escenas.dice: Vienna, eighteen twenty-four. A composer who can't hear premieres his last symphony.
Ludwig van Beethoven is almost completely deaf. He stands by the stage anyway, beating time for an orchestra he can't hear.
The players were told to ignore him and follow the other conductor.
At the end, the story goes, he's still conducting. A singer has to turn him around,
and only then does he see the audience applauding.
The finale of that symphony is Ode to Joy. Today it's the anthem of Europe.
Want to play it this week? Every note has its letter printed inside, so you just find the key.

Vienna, May 7, 1824. Ludwig van Beethoven, almost completely deaf, stands by the stage at the premiere of his Ninth Symphony, beating time for an orchestra he can't hear. The players had been told to follow the other conductor. At the end (accounts differ on the exact moment) he is still conducting, and the contralto Caroline Unger turns him around to see the audience applauding. The symphony's finale, Ode to Joy, was adopted as the Anthem of Europe in 1972.
